description.narrative: Den nya insatsen syftar till att bidra till minskade växthusgaser inom avfallssektorn genom att främja hanteringsmodeller under en cirkulär ekonomi. Huvudmålet är inriktat på att konsolidera och replikera modeller för hantering av fast avfall, metoder och verktyg i en mellanstor stad genom att utnyttja resurser och artikulera offentliga (nationella och lokala) såväl som privata initiativ.

The new intervention wants to contribute to the reduction of greenhouse gases in the waste subsector through the promotion of management models under a circular economy approach. The main objective is oriented to consolidate and replicate solid waste management models, approaches and tools in a major an intermediate city by leveraging resources and articulating public initiatives (national and local), as well as private initiatives.

General Objective: Project Impact Contribute to the reduction of greenhouse gases and preservation of ecosystems in the waste subsector through the development of management models with a circular economy approach.
Specific objective: project purpose Consolidate and replicate solid waste management models, approaches and tools in a major city and an intermediate city by leveraging resources and articulating public initiatives (national and local), as well as private initiatives.
Results framework For the second phase, a support component for national policies is proposed, with the objective of scaling up the lessons learned from the project to national public policies (Outcome 1); a second component dedicated to the new municipalities of intervention (Outcome 2) and finally a component dedicated to knowledge management focused on the consolidation of actions in the municipalities of intervention of the first phase and the systematization of experiences of the second phase, in order to capitalize and systematize the good practices and lessons learned (Outcome 3).

description.narrative: During the 2024 period, the main results achieved so far are: At the national level, with the Ministry of Environment and Water and the Plurinational Authority of Mother Earth: • i) National solid waste diagnosis; ii) National Inventory of Dumps, iii) Technical Guide for the Closure of Dumps and iv) Technical Guide for the Design and Operation of Manual Sanitary Landfills. • Preparation of the Waste Co-processing Regulations and Formation of the Technical Co-Processing Committee • Instrument for measuring greenhouse gases in the waste sector during the operation of sanitation and final disposal services and during the processes of preparing pre-investment studies (ITCP) and investment studies (EDTP). •Support in the implementation of the extended producer responsibility (EPR) regime through the diagnosis of PET containers and pesticide containers. At the local level, with the Autonomous Municipal Government of Oruro: • Municipal Program for Integrated Waste Management (PMGIR) • Construction of the municipal policy for the inclusion of grassroots recyclers • Optimization of organic waste collection and treatment processes in markets, • Composting Center Improvements • Construction of two collection centers for recyclable waste • Technical closure plan for the Huajara Dump; • Reengineering of the mechanical classification line of the Oruro Mechanical Biological Treatment Plant; • Reengineering of the Urban Sanitation Service (SAU), a study that will expand the spatial coverage of collection services to 95% and sweeping services to 80%, in 2025 the operation of the new sanitation service will begin. Actions to consolidate the models of the first phase: • Accompaniment to the municipal governments of Tarija and La Paz in the models generated during the first phase. In La Paz, in coordination with the cement company Soboce, pilot co-processing tests for the green energy transition have been carried out. •In addition, the Camiri GAM has been assisted in the management of financing the Project for the Camiri Waste Treatment Complex and coordination with the Ministry of Environment and Water, achieving its incorporation into the new IDB credit operation of the BO-L1237 Program, which is in the approval phase by the Plurinational Legislative Assembly, ensuring external financing of approximately 19 million bolivianos for its implementation.
